children: Canadian biotech QurCan Therapeutics on Tuesday announced an investment from Eli Lilly
as part of an exclusive research and collaboration agreement with the Indiana-based pharma giant to develop genetic medicines.
The deal focuses on leveraging QurCan’s TERP (Target-Engineered Responsive Polymer) platform to develop genetic medicines that target the central and peripheral nervous systems.
Under the agreement, QurCan will lead the initial research, after which Eli Lilly
will take over further research, clinical development, and commercialization.
The Toronto-based firm will receive an upfront payment and a strategic investment from Lilly

as part of the deal. Additionally, the company will be entitled to a per-program payment of up to $237M, which represents R&D support payments as well as research, development, and commercial milestone payments.
QurCan will also receive tiered royalties as a percentage of global net sales of commercialized products.
